 Apple just revealed the iPad Mini I’ve always wanted. But is it worth the new price?
 By Mike Andronico , CNN Underscored
 Published
 10:29 AM EDT, Mon October 26, 2026
 Link Copied!
 Apple 
 In this article 
 The iPad Mini finally goes OLED 
 The takeaway 
 FAQs 
 Why trust CNN Underscored 
 In a packed month that’s seen Apple drop the iPhone Duo and Apple HomeView , it’s the revamped iPad Mini that actually has me the most excited. This long-awaited update finally brings an OLED screen to Apple’s smallest tablet, alongside a slimmer, water-resistant design and the promise of faster performance than ever.
 But like so many recent Apple products , it’s also $100 more expensive than before. The new iPad Mini goes up for preorder this Wednesday (Oct. 28) ahead of its Nov. 6 release date, and you might be wondering if it’s time for you to upgrade. With that said, here’s why I’m eager to get my hands on Apple’s tiny OLED tablet, and who I think it might actually be for.
 Apple iPad Mini (2026) 
 Apple 
 The new iPad Mini brings an OLED display to Apple's smallest tablet in addition to a slimmer, water-resistant design and the power of the new A20 Pro chip.
 From $699 at Apple
 The iPad Mini finally goes OLED
 The new iPad Mini’s headline feature is its 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display, which is a tiny bit bigger than the previous-generation 8.3-inch Mini and should offer significantly richer color and contrast compared to what we’ve seen before. It also offers the option of a nano-texture display covering on the 256GB and 512GB models, which we’ve tested on other Apple screens such as the iMac and could be great for minimizing glare when you’re out reading in the sun. I’m bummed that the iPad Mini still doesn’t have Apple’s ProMotion tech for extra-smooth scrolling and swiping, but the addition of OLED is a major wishlist item that brings it one step closer to being the small iPad Pro some folks may want.
 Apple 
 But the new Mini has more than OLED going for it. It’s even slimmer and lighter than before, and perhaps more significantly, is the first iPad Mini to carry an IP67 rating for water resistance — something that could prove crucial when you want to catch up on your Netflix queue by the pool. It also packs what Apple is calling an “Acoustic Display” that effectively pairs the speakers directly behind the screen for “punchier bass and more volume” and allows for that sealed enclosure that keeps the Mini safe around water.
 Another long overdue change? The 12MP Center Stage camera is now centered on the horizontal edge, which should make the iPad Mini much more ideal for FaceTiming friends and hopping on Zoom calls. Unfortunately, there’s one small step backward on the design front: the latest iPad Mini only comes in Midnight and Starlight color options, ditching the more vibrant blue and purple hues from the last model.
 The new iPad Mini is powered by the same Apple’s A20 Pro chip found in the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, which delivered some of the best performance of any mobile devices we’ve tested and should deliver a significant leap over the still-strong A17 iPad Mini . Apple is once again promising up to 10 hours of battery life (a number that the previous iPad Mini exceeded on our own tests), and support for both the Apple Pencil USB-C and Apple Pencil Pro. Just don’t expect features like Split View and Stage Manager for multitasking; those are still exclusive to the iPad Air and iPad Pro tablets that are powered by the more muscular M-series chips.
 The takeaway
 Apple 
 The iPad Mini has long been my favorite iPad since it’s the perfect size for binging comics and watching TV shows and movies on the go, and I can’t wait to get my hands on an even slimmer model with a (hopefully) gorgeous OLED screen. And after years of calling each new iPad Mini a strong but boring upgrade, I’m glad to see Apple make some noteworthy design changes that should make both first-time iPad owners and enthusiast upgraders happy.
 That said, this new tablet arrives in the wake of the iPhone Duo, which has replaced the iPad Mini for a lot of my big-screen needs when I’m commuting. Sure, its 7.4-inch OLED screen isn’t as big as the Mini’s 8.5-inch display, but the convenience of only having to carry one device is hard to beat. And while many apps still need to be optimized for the Duo’s bigger screen, Apple’s foldable phone allows for actual split-screen multitasking that the iPad Mini still can’t pull off. I realize this is a niche recommendation, but if you’re among the people who splurged for Apple’s $2,000 phone, you probably don’t need an iPad Mini.
 Still, I’m eager to see if the Mini’s bigger, richer display and revamped design can once again give me a reason to keep a dedicated tablet on me. We’ll be getting our hands on one as soon as possible, so stay tuned for our full review.
 FAQs
 What's the iPad Mini 8's price and release date?
 The iPad Mini 8 goes up for preorder on Oct. 28 and is set to hit stores on Nov. 6. The tablet starts at $699 with 128GB of storage, though you can upgrade to a $799 model with a 256GB and a $999 model with 512GB. Both the 256GB and 512GB models feature nano-texture displays that help mitigate glare.
 What are the big differences between the iPad Mini 8 and iPad Mini 7
 The latest iPad Mini is a significant upgrade over its predecessor, starting with its 8.5-inch OLED display that’s both bigger and more vibrant than the 8.3-inch LED display on the previous Mini. It’s a little thinner and lighter, has water resistance for the first time and packs an A20 Pro processor that should deliver notably faster speeds than the A17 chip in the seventh-generation model. Unfortunately, the new iPad Mini is limited to just Midnight and Starlight color options, ditching the blue and purple from last generation.
